lines.text: What if every American state became its own country, and they all went to war?
California has the people: 39 million, and an economy bigger than Japan's.
lines.say: California has the people. Thirty-nine million, and an economy bigger than Japan's.

lines.text: Texas has the oil: more than 40 percent of America's supply.
lines.say: Texas has the oil. More than forty percent of America's supply.

lines.text: Virginia has the navy: the largest naval base in the world, and the only shipyard that builds aircraft carriers.
lines.say: Virginia has the navy. The largest naval base in the world, and the only shipyard that builds aircraft carriers.

lines.text: So who wins? Take a guess.
Day one: Texas turns off the oil. Within weeks, California's freeways are empty and the Midwest can't run its tractors.
lines.say: Day one. Texas turns off the oil. Within weeks, California's freeways are empty, and the Midwest can't run its tractors.

lines.text: Then the farm states stop the trains. Iowa and Illinois grow the corn; California grows half the country's fruit and vegetables. Nobody can feed themselves alone.
lines.say: Then the farm states stop the trains. Iowa and Illinois grow the corn. California grows half the country's fruit and vegetables. Nobody can feed themselves alone.

lines.text: Virginia's fleet blockades the coasts, but every ship needs Texas fuel and Midwest grain.
And then everyone remembers the missiles. All 400 of America's land-based nuclear missiles sit in three states: Wyoming, Montana and North Dakota, with fewer people than Brooklyn between them.
lines.say: And then everyone remembers the missiles. All four hundred of America's land-based nuclear missiles sit in three states. Wyoming, Montana and North Dakota, with fewer people than Brooklyn between them.

lines.text: So the winner is the three states nobody looked at. And since everyone knows it, the war never starts.
